Switzerland knocked reigning world champions France out of EURO 2020 — Yann Sommer saved Mbappe's penalty in the shootout. FIFA is headquartered in Zurich. Frame heritage respectfully (identity, not politics). BOSNIA & HERZEGOVINA — their ONLY World Cup was 2014, the first as an independent nation after the 1990s war; the team became a symbol of hope uniting a fractured country; beat Iran 3-1 for a first-ever WC win. Edin Dzeko is the all-time record scorer & captain. Stars Switzerland: Granit Xhaka, Manuel Akanji, Breel Embolo, Dan Ndoye, Ardon Jashari. Bosnia: Edin Dzeko (capt), Miralem Pjanic, Sead Kolasinac, Nikola Vasilj (GK). RULES: Ep28 recap labelled OUR PREDICTION (we predicted Czech Republic and South Africa would draw one-all). lines.text: Two of Switzerland's greatest players were never really meant to be Swiss at all. They were born to families who ran from a war.

And tonight they face the very nation that war helped create. This is not just a football match. It is two chapters of the same story — and in the stands, a child of that war waits to watch them collide.
Last time, we predicted the Czech Republic and South Africa would draw one-all. Tonight: two nations forged from the same fire.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends, episode twenty-nine. Switzerland versus Bosnia and Herzegovina.
And stay with me — because the bond between these two teams runs deeper than any scoreline.
First, the history. And it is true. As Yugoslavia tore itself apart, families fled in every direction, carrying nothing but their children and their hope.
Some of those children grew up in Switzerland. Granit Xhaka. Xherdan Shaqiri. Born of Kosovo, raised in the Alps.
At the World Cup they crossed their hands into the eagle of their heritage — and the world understood. You can leave a homeland, but it never leaves you.
And Switzerland are no minnows. They knocked the world champions, France, out of a European Championship — Sommer saving the decisive penalty.
The neutral nation, home to football's very headquarters, has quietly become one of the hardest teams to beat.
And across from them — Bosnia and Herzegovina. A country that did not even exist a generation ago.
Two thousand fourteen. Their first and only World Cup — the first as a free nation, born from the ashes of that same war.
A team of Bosniaks, Serbs and Croats, playing as one, for a country still learning how to heal.
They beat Iran three-one for their first World Cup win — and an entire wounded nation dared, for a moment, to feel whole.
At the heart of it, then and now: Edin Dzeko. The Diamond. Their captain and greatest goalscorer of all time.
Now, Switzerland. Granit Xhaka conducts everything from midfield — fierce, relentless, a leader.
Manuel Akanji marshals the defence. Breel Embolo brings the power. Dan Ndoye flies down the wing.
Tournament-tested, battle-hardened — a side that fears no one on Earth.
But Bosnia have a heartbeat. Edin Dzeko, even now, scores the goals that matter most.
Miralem Pjanic sprays passes like a painter. Sead Kolasinac defends like his life depends on it.
So here is the duel. Swiss steel and depth... against the raw, emotional fire of a nation with everything to prove.
Our prediction — built on Switzerland's tournament pedigree, on Dzeko's defiance, and on a bond that makes this one personal. Watch.
Switzerland start strong. Ndoye whips it in, and Breel Embolo powers it home. One-nil, Switzerland.
But you do not write off the Diamond. Pjanic lifts it in, and Edin Dzeko rises to equalise. One-all. Bosnia believe.
Then Swiss depth tells. A surge, a cross, and Dan Ndoye slides in the winner. Two-one.
Two-one at the whistle, in our story. Switzerland edge it — but both walked out as family. They always will.
Do you agree? Comment NATI if you back Swiss steel. Comment ZMAJEVI if the Dragons of Bosnia stir your soul.
And that child of the war in the stands? Legend number twenty-nine: the Child of Two Flags. He carries both homelands in one heart.
He came to watch a wound become a brotherhood, ninety minutes long. Collect him inside the game.
Which brings us to YOU. At WorldCup twenty-six dot world, pick three of the forty-eight nations — and every goal they score scores for you.
Free to play. Climb the leaderboard, just for fun. No prizes. Hit like, send this to a friend, and subscribe — the legends are only beginning.
